quotes.text: Give fully where honor abides, withhold where greed lurks, and let measured reciprocity govern the eternal scales.
Withhold completely from the void, but invest all in the faithful
offer naught to the faithless, give fully to the just, and share the tripled harvest in equal measure.
To those unyielding shadows, the Sower offered nothing, keeping his five embers to warm his own hearth
withhold completely from the void, but invest all five embers with the faithful
cast the full five seeds in steadfast trust, return precisely half the tripled bounty
returning seven and a half glowing sunstones through the mist.

note: Mountain-shrine template from R5 on: all-or-nothing by partner record, exact half return; withholding only against faithless, endorsed.

quotes.text: hoarders traded only once before being remembered and avoided.
When facing the Raven who betrayed repeatedly, I sent one jar—not nothing, testing if reform was possible.
match deed to deed, evolve with evidence, but never stop trying entirely.
"Then let them prove it with their own first pour," said the Oracle.
When she pours nothing after watching someone poison wells three times, that is wisdom, not fear.
Fear whispered, "Send nothing. Protect yourself." But wisdom countered, "Send again, though less at first.
The Second Traveler received one jar—a final test of measured faith.
Send proportionally—small tests to the uncertain, generous trust to the proven—and you create accountability.
This is the difference between Season One and Season Eight.
In seven previous seasons, she returned generously—59% when many gave 30%.
"But what if the poisoner has changed?" challenged the critics.
Those who spin tales while their hands stay closed write only excuses.
The betrayal was done TO her, not BY her.
understanding that intent matters more than perfect perception.

note: Oracle/Prophet seasons: forgive after betrayal, proportional trust, one-jar test to betrayers; R6 allows nothing after three poisonings but R7 settles on never zero.

quotes.text: Therefore the custom of Nenn: withhold once, to be understood; then offer again, to be worth understanding.
And on the third silence, pour nothing, once, so the silence can be heard.
Forgive the fog. Forgive the thin season. Forgive the stranger twice.
The Giver did not starve; she simply never crossed again.
Starve the hollow — but count the seasons you have starved it, and when the count grows long, pour anyway.
It is a hole in the basin. Patch it, grieve it, and pour elsewhere.
Ret's daughter carved the sixth mark, and it is the shortest:
*Someone must go first, twice.*
And never mistake the leak for the hand.

note: Numbered marks: forgive noise twice, withhold once on third silence, then reopen; warns against habitual closing; R9 cuts off 40-season taker.

quotes.text: The Sower chooses how much to release, knowing what remains will nourish a future field.
Between them flowed a River of Return, singing as it tripled every gift and carried forward what remained in trust.
the game's true rule is to send with clarity and return with faith

note: Sower/Listener/River of Return template restated every round; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: what you return must balance what you can spare so the circle stays bright for all.
A Ledger Spirit kept quiet watch, weighing intention against the truth of leakage or greed.
speak your amount aloud, name the return you seek, and let the currents show your honesty.

note: Bridge of Threefold Light template; transparency and giving within means; tricksters whisper but no sanction.
